title: introduce per-shard async request queues and affinity hints to eliminate global serializer bottleneck
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: We observed a recurring CPU-side serialization hotspot in the request path when contention rises on the global serializer used to serialize request context, route lookups and KV-cache lookups. This PR replaces the single global serializer with per-shard asynchronous request queues, pushes KV-cache lookup heavyweight work off the network accept threads, and replaces strict thread pinning with lightweight affinity hints to reduce cross-core thrashing. Summary of changes: 1) Introduces RequestShard and ShardQueue: each shard has a lock-free MPSC queue that accepts lightweight request handles; workers pull requests and perform scheduling and kernel/eviction decisions. 2) Replaces global request serialization lock with per-request object sequencing and fence-free handoff via atomic states. 3) KV-cache fast path now does a batched probe step: on admission requests are grouped by shard, batched KV probes happen on local shard workers to exploit cache locality and reduce page faults. 4) Heavy synchronous operations (model weights load/quantize, cold KV misses) are offloaded to a background worker pool with backpressure tokens so latency-sensitive workers are never blocked. 5) Threading model tuned: removed strict cpu_set pinning in favor of affinity hints and a hop-count aware scheduling heuristic to prefer hot-shard locality without preventing OS migration. 6) Added observability: shard-level counters, per-step histograms (enqueue latency, queue-to-worker latency, kv-probe time), and a dashboard link. Performance impact: internal perf lab benchmarks for a mixed-inference workload with 32 concurrent clients show median tail savings: p50 latency -4.2%, p95 -9.6%, p99 -18.3% and sustained throughput +11% before hitting GPU saturation. CPU utilization traces show the global serialization spike eliminated and worker core CPU variance reduced by ~36%. Testing and validation: unit tests for ShardQueue and RequestShard ordering, integration tests that simulate KV-cache hot/cold ratios, and a rollout canary across 10% of dedicated capacity clusters passed with no increased error rate. Rollout plan: phased canary, observe shard-level metrics for 48 hours, then increment to 50% and full roll when no regressions. Related tickets: ENG-982 request path serialization, ENG-987 kv-cache eviction scheduling. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks - [x] Observability panels updated - [x] Canary plan and rollback steps. Commits summary: see commits list below. Files touched: core/scheduler/shard_queue.rs, core/scheduler/mod.rs, core/kv/cache.rs, core/kv/eviction.rs, runtime/threading/affinity.rs, runtime/metrics/shard_metrics.rs, tests/integration/kv_shard_integration.rs, docs/observability/shard_dashboard.md. Merge outcome: squash merge into main with commit message that summarizes the shard queue and affinity hint changes. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to ordering guarantees in RequestShard, eviction interaction with batched probes, and backpressure token correctness for the background pool. If issues arise we can toggle the per-shard routing off via runtime flag.

review_comments: Jun Park: The lock-free MPSC queue looks good but please add comments explaining the ABA avoidance strategy used in pop(), response: added comments and a unit test to demonstrate ABA case coverage.
Aisha Khan: Can we measure the impact of affinity hints in noisy multi-tenant nodes? response: added a noisy-node integration test and observed consistent improvements; documented in perf notes.

Liam O'Connor: Concern about eviction ordering when batching probes across shards, response: updated eviction logic to preserve per-request eviction-scoring timestamps and added an integration test to validate ordering.
release_notes: Server runtime: Reduced CPU-side request serialization by replacing a global serializer with per-shard async queues. Improved tail latency and throughput under contention. Opt-in rollout behind runtime flag. Observability added for shard-level scheduling metrics.
